(a) SBIR.—Section 9(m) of the Small Business Act (15 U.S.C. 638(m)) is amended by striking “September 30, 2017” and inserting “September 30, 2022”. 
    (b) STTR.—Section 9(n)(1) of the Small Business Act (15 U.S.C. 638(n)(1)) is amended by striking “fiscal year 2017” and inserting “fiscal year 2022”.

fable.w: This section only extends the sunset dates of the SBIR and STTR programs by swapping dates in the Small Business Act. The tempting reading is that these programs involve small businesses, which are outside the federal government, but the text sets up no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue. Small businesses applying for program awards would not count as participation in any case.

qwen_block.w: This section merely extends the expiration dates for the Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) and Small Business Technology Transfer (STTR) programs. It does not establish any process for public comment, consultation with outside entities, or advisory boards. It is a simple statutory amendment regarding program authorization timelines.
qwen_block.s: Section 9(m) of the Small Business Act (15 U.S.C. 638(m)) is amended by striking “September 30, 2017” and inserting “September 30, 2022”.

opus.w: This section only extends the termination dates of the SBIR and STTR programs by replacing "September 30, 2017" and "fiscal year 2017" with 2022 dates. It creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside entities, rulemaking authority, or right to sue. The link to small businesses is a trap: their role in these programs is applying for awards, which is excluded, and this text doesn't touch that process anyway.
opus.b:
**Step 1: Analysis**

The tempting reading is that this is participation because SBIR and STTR are programs where small businesses (outside parties) take part in federal research funding. That fails for two reasons. First, the section itself only swaps termination dates (2017 to 2022) and involves no outside party in any federal decision. Second, even the underlying programs work through applications for awards, which the definition excludes.

qwen_chat.w: This section merely amends the expiration dates for the Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) and Small Business Technology Transfer (STTR) programs. It does not establish any new process for public participation, consultation, or coordination with outside entities. The text contains no requirements for hearings, comment periods, or advisory committees involving non-federal parties.
qwen_chat.s:
(a) SBIR.—Section 9(m) of the Small Business Act (15 U.S.C. 638(m)) is amended by striking “September 30, 2017” and inserting “September 30, 2022”. 
    (b) STTR.—Section 9(n)(1) of the Small Business Act (15 U.S.C. 638(n)(1)) is amended by striking “fiscal year 2017” and inserting “fiscal year 2022”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that extending the authorization for SBIR and STTR programs implies continued interaction with small businesses and research institutions. However, the text itself only changes dates; it does not describe any specific participatory mechanism (like a hearing, comment period, or advisory board) within this section. The section is purely an amendment to the expiration dates of existing programs.
